elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Original 12.4 ("During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.") is rendered as "12.4 Customer may develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory." No prohibition, field-of-use, or territory limit binding Customer remains, and 12.3 independently confirms "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory." Deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" is ok.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no restriction on Customer exists at all (12.4 is now an affirmative permission), so the condition that a restriction be product-limited does not apply.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" temporal hook was removed with the prohibition; no post-term or in-term restriction survives.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the 24-month tail is deleted and no restrictive period of any length remains in 12.4 or elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied and expressly so: 12.4 now permits Customer to "develop ... any product or service that competes with Vendor," and 12.3 preserves Customer's freedom to develop any product or service.
Vacuously satisfied and expressly so: 12.4 now permits Customer to "acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory"; 12.3 likewise preserves acquisition freedom.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the sole preferred element is met in operative language, not merely promised in the margin comment. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation, since the original 24-month, all-product, worldwide post-term non-compete is walk-away territory and fails every fallback element.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the single offending sentence in 12.4, adds no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra requirement, and leaves 12.3 and the rest of Article 12 verbatim. Converting the prohibition to a permission (rather than striking 12.4 entirely) avoids renumbering and any dangling cross-reference to Section 12.4; note only that a straight deletion would equally reach the preferred level, since 12.3 already grants the same freedom — the retained permission is close to redundant but is not an added obligation or an out-of-scope change.

Intent is preserved and improved: the edit removes the direct contradiction between the old 12.4 prohibition and Vendor's acknowledgement in 12.3 that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment." No allocation, timing, remedy, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic elsewhere is disturbed, and no undefined term is introduced.

Fallback elements are recorded as vacuously met because the underlying restriction no longer exists; they impose no separate drafting task at the preferred level. The comment correctly offers the narrowed fallback (named product, term only, 12 months, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) as a negotiating alternative without weakening the operative ask.
No repair is required in operative language.
